headers._comment: Only Vite's output gets the immutable year — those filenames contain a content hash, so a changed file is always a new URL.

A team board is the same index.html, reached at /t/<token> — and a header rule matches the REQUESTED path, not the file a rewrite lands on. So the board fell through to the default hour of caching while the app itself was no-cache, and a parent's phone kept serving a page from up to an hour ago. The board's DATA is read live from Firestore either way; what was stale was the app around it.

The service worker decides whether a notification arrives at all, and its name never changes — so an hour of default caching is an hour in which a fix does not reach a phone. Browsers re-check it on their own schedule; this makes sure the re-check actually gets the new file.
The home-screen icons and the manifest have stable names. An immutable year here would pin every phone to today's icon for a year, with no way to correct it.
